article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Evening Brief
article.dek: Monday night's inactive lists are final with Charbonnet and Price active for Seattle, Baltimore's quarterback room thins further before Thursday night, and the board's cards are unchanged from this morning because its evening refresh had not landed.

items.headline: Lead: Monday night inactives are final — Charbonnet and Price active for Seattle
paragraphs: The inactive lists for Chicago at Seattle are final, so the last pre-kickoff unknown is settled. Seattle has running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price active — Charbonnet for the first time since tearing his ACL last postseason, Price for the first time since Week 3 after coming off injured reserve. Newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson debuts for Seattle, and newly acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons debuts for Chicago.

Seattle is without left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), backup quarterback Drew Lock (elbow), running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), defensive tackle Brandon Pili (back), and guard Beau Stephens. Chicago is without running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for a fourth straight game and cornerback Malik Muhammad II (toe), plus emergency quarterback Case Keenum, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden, and defensive tackles Jayden Loving and Jordan van den Berg. Chicago linebacker D'Marco Jackson, listed questionable, is active.
Chicago at Seattle kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET. The inactive lists were the last pre-kickoff update, and they are in.
items.takeaway: Monday night inactives are final: Charbonnet and Price active for Seattle, Nelson and Simmons debuting, and Cross, Shaheed, Nwosu, Monangai, and Muhammad out.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Baltimore's quarterback room thins further before Thursday night
paragraphs: Baltimore's Monday walkthrough made the Thursday night picture clearer, and it is not good for the Ravens. Tyler Huntley did not participate with his toe injury, and reports say he is set to miss extended time — not just Thursday against Jacksonville. Lamar Jackson did not participate either, with the right thumb injury that requires surgery and a move to injured reserve.

That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who finished Sunday's loss at Buffalo, as the next man up — but he was limited Monday with an ankle injury of his own. He has said he hopes to play Thursday. Baltimore signed quarterback Austin Reed to the practice squad Monday as cover.

One more Baltimore note: kicker Tyler Loop did not participate with a groin injury, and Jake Moody is expected to kick Thursday. Baltimore's quarterback for Thursday is still not officially named, so watch the next injury reports — but do not expect Huntley.
items.takeaway: Huntley did not practice and is set to miss extended time, Fagnano was limited with an ankle injury, and Baltimore signed Austin Reed as cover for Thursday.

items.headline: Weather: cool and calm for Monday night in Seattle
paragraphs: Monday night in Seattle looks cool and calm. The hourly forecast has about 50 degrees around the 5:15 p.m. local kickoff window, partly cloudy skies, a light north-northwest wind of about 2 mph, and a 15 percent chance of rain, with temperatures holding around 48 to 49 degrees through the evening.
That is the forecast as it stands Monday evening, reported as fact. It is not a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: Seattle Monday night: about 50 degrees at kickoff, partly cloudy, light wind, 15 percent rain chance.

items.headline: Evening cards: Seattle moneyline on top, Chicago +3 fills both other cards
paragraphs: The board had not yet picked up its evening refresh when this brief was built, so these are the same cards as this morning — see Line Movement for what that means.

Hit Rate is the Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET against Chicago. It is the pick the app rates most likely to win, with a model probability of 0.561. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. A favorite's moneyline can look safe and still pay very little — you are betting on the outright winner only.
Balanced is Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value is Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings as well — the same pick as Balanced. Value is always the model's +EV play, and that play and the Balanced play land on the same line. Two cards pointing at the same pick is not two separate bets; it is one pick the app likes two ways.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Seattle moneyline -175. Balanced and Value: both Chicago +3 -102 at DraftKings — one pick, liked two ways.

items.headline: A card that changes still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at their listed books. If your book is not that book, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers
paragraphs: Key numbers are the most common margins of victory in football, and 3 is the biggest one. Games land on 3 more than any other margin because so many games are decided by a single field goal.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a spread moves from -3 to -2.5. That half-point matters more than it looks, because a favorite that wins by exactly 3 now covers instead of pushing. The same half-point on a spread of -7.5 to -7 matters less, because 7 is less common than 3 — but it still matters.

That is why a line move across a key number is worth more attention than a move that stays between them. When you run a price through Check, the app prices the line you actually have — including which side of a key number it sits on.
items.takeaway: Three is football's most common winning margin, so a spread crossing 3 — or a half-point around it — is worth more than most other moves.

items.headline: Evening board still shows the morning cards — refresh had not landed at read time
paragraphs: When this brief was built, the board had not yet picked up its evening refresh, so it still showed the morning cards: Hit Rate on the Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings, and Balanced and Value both on Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings. That is a refresh timing note, not a claim that no book moved during the day.

Because the board had not refreshed, there is no new card movement to report between the morning and evening reads. The last real movement on this game was the morning board's: the Seattle moneyline getting pricier from -166 to -175, and Chicago +3 moving from FanDuel to DraftKings at the same -102.
If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you. Your book's price is the one that matters.
items.takeaway: No new card movement at the evening read — the board had not refreshed since morning, so the cards are unchanged: Seattle moneyline -175, Chicago +3 -102.

items.headline: Monday game? Monday check.
paragraphs: The one thing worth waiting for today is done: Monday night's inactive lists are final. There is no pending injury event left on this game, so there is no reason to wait on that account.

One honest note while you are here: settlement in the tracker is manual, and it only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds wins is not a record, it is a highlight reel.
items.takeaway: Inactives are final, so nothing is left to wait for — and log the losers too, or the tracker is not a record.
